feedback.problem:
Find the standard matrix that  represents  the  linear  transformation $T:{R}^{3}\to {R}^{2},$ where
$T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}-3x-5y+2z \\ 2x-3y\end{aligned}].$
feedback.worked_solution:
We require a $2\times 3$ matrix $T$ such that
    

$$
T\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}(-3)x+(-5)y+2z \\ 2x+(-3)y+0z\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that
    

$$
[\begin{aligned}-3 & -5 & 2 \\ 2 & -3 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3x-5y+2z \\ 2x-3y\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the matrix which represents the linear transformation $T$ is
    

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-3 & -5 & 2 \\ 2 & -3 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$
